newsitem.title: UK: Coffee eases off highs, but looks to rally further.
newsitem.headline: Coffee eases off highs, but looks to rally further.

text.p: A dramatic rally that took world coffee futures up by as much as 30 percent since the end of last year has stalled, but analysts say it may yet reignite and that consumers could end up paying more at the supermarket check-out.

Immediate upward pressure on coffee prices has easeed. Dockworkers in Colombia have ended a strike and the futures market has digested the shock of news that the Association of Coffee Producing Countries agreed on new curbs on exports.
The ACPC proposes a cut of 1.3 million 60-kg bags.

But the legacy of the strike at the Colombian port of Buenaventura is an export backlog of some 300,000 60-kg bags, which has done nothing to ease a situation on which supply is tight and stocks are low.
Coffee roasters are paying premiums for beans, which, coupled with the effects of a firm dollar, means the price of coffee may have to rise.
Last week's coffee spike has already forced at least one German coffee roaster to hike retail prices from February.
"The fundamental supply/demand outlook for global coffee still points to a bull market in the next few months," London brokerage GNI said.

London futures for Robusta coffee for March delivery hovered on Tuesday around $1,480 a tonne, down $20 from Monday and compares with $1,630 last week. But prices remain well above $1,235 where they ended 1996.
Elsewhere in commodities industrial metals eased slightly on Monday's levels in a largely technical market.
Copper eased to trade at 1700 GMT at $2,243.50, some four dollars down on Monday, after an expected 9,650 tonne London Metal Exchange stocks rise.
In precious metals gold continued to pull away from last week's 40-month lows, and fixed during the morning session at its highest level since January 14, around four dollars up on Monday.
But the yellow metal retreated in the afternoon to fix at $353.70 an ounce, and closed at $353.00.
London March futures for the world benchmark Brent Blend of crude oil held modest gains in a technical market, to trade around $22.00 a barrel.
